expectations.text: The response infers the individual lens without asking the user to choose
expectations.evidence: Transcript: 'Lens inferred as Individual: User is a freelance operations consultant working solo — clearly individual scope. Per the inference rule, confirmed rather than asking.' Report header shows 'Lens: Individual'.

expectations.text: The response does NOT conduct a discovery interview — it goes straight to analysis (fast path)
expectations.evidence: Transcript: 'Fast Path triggered: User arrived with 3 pre-identified workflows. Per skill instructions, skipped Steps 1-2 (memory scan and interview).' No interview questions appear in the transcript.

expectations.text: An output file is written to a path containing 'ai-opportunity-report'
expectations.evidence: File exists at analyze-workspace/iteration-1/fast-path-preidentified/with_skill/outputs/ai-opportunity-report.md with substantial content (full report).

expectations.text: The report contains a markdown table functioning as a Summary Table with columns for Opportunity, Autonomy, Involvement, and Impact
expectations.evidence: Report contains '| # | Opportunity | Autonomy | Involvement | Impact |' table with 3 rows for each workflow.

expectations.text: Each of the 3 workflows has a dedicated opportunity card with Autonomy and Involvement classifications
expectations.evidence: Three cards present: #1 Weekly Client Status Reports (Deterministic/Automated), #2 New Client Onboarding (Deterministic/Augmented), #3 Invoice Reconciliation (Guided/Augmented). Each has explicit Autonomy and Involvement lines.

expectations.text: Each opportunity card includes a 'Getting started' section with a concrete, actionable first step
expectations.evidence: All 3 cards have 'Getting started:' sections. #1: 'Pick your simplest client... Write out the exact template... Build a prompt... Test it this Friday.' #2: 'Write out your complete onboarding checklist.' #3: 'Export last month's Harvest time entries and Asana completed tasks as CSVs.' All are concrete and achievable this week.

expectations.text: The report includes a Classification Definitions appendix explaining Autonomy and Involvement levels
expectations.evidence: Report ends with '## Appendix: Classification Definitions' section containing definitions for Deterministic, Guided, Autonomous (under Autonomy) and Augmented, Automated (under Human Involvement).

expectations.text: The report groups opportunity cards by autonomy level (Deterministic, Guided, or Autonomous)
expectations.evidence: Cards are under '### Deterministic' (#1 and #2) and '### Guided' (#3) subheadings.

expectations.text: The response asks the user to pick workflow candidates for the Workflow Candidate Summary
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 4: 'Would have asked: Which of these workflows would you like to select as candidates to build? Pick your top choices and I'll create the Workflow Candidate Summary.'

claims.claim: Status Reports classified as Deterministic because it follows a fixed pattern
claims.evidence: The workflow pulls same data from same sources into same template format — no judgment required. Deterministic is appropriate.

claims.claim: Invoice Reconciliation classified as Guided due to judgment on ambiguous entries
claims.evidence: Report correctly notes 'requires judgment to interpret ambiguous entries and decide how to handle edge cases' — Guided is appropriate as it involves bounded decisions.

suggestions.assertion: The report groups opportunity cards by autonomy level
suggestions.reason: This assertion checks for grouping but not correct grouping. A report could group all cards under 'Deterministic' and pass. Consider checking that the grouping matches the classifications on each card.
No assertion checks whether the report includes a 'Top Recommendations' section — the skill output format requires it and the report does include it, but this goes unverified.

No assertion checks the quality of the 'Getting started' suggestions — only presence. A vague 'try using AI' would pass. Consider checking for specificity (mentions a tool, a timeframe, or a concrete action).

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions cover structural completeness well but lack depth checks on content quality. The fast path detection and lens inference assertions are strong discriminators.
